scope: Read-only inspection of the frozen r1 production implementation and its actual existing test output. No production edits, test execution, device actions or plan status changes by this reviewer.

findings.title: A parent object patch can succeed while an existing scalar descendant silently wins
findings.reproduction: Set cas.document.name="old" through the production legacy setter, read the local revision, then conditionally set cas.document={"name":"new"}. The merge produces new in the parent record, but materializeJson replays the existing scalar child record afterwards. Its newer-parent exception applies only to object leaves, so the effective value remains old.
findings.required_change: Compose field intent against the existing owning CRDT records, including null/array replacement and deletion, or reject a genuinely ambiguous overlap explicitly. Do not change the distributed storage model silently. Add real production parent/child tests.

findings.title: The preview is not actually validated as a complete effective candidate
findings.reproduction: With call.indoor.return_s=30, set call.indoor.return_s.inner=1 through the conditional API. The existing per-key validator recognizes the exact return_s path and known containers but not this deeper path, while materialization turns the numeric field into an object. The temporary cfg does not help because the loop still validates the original mutation key/value only. doors.front.unlock.command.inner has the same shape.
findings.required_change: Validate affected known schema roots against the actual materialized candidate, preserving unrelated unknown extensions and the existing secret contract. Include a rejected deep-leaf injection test and assert no config or revision publication.

findings.title: New configuration C ABI methods can dereference an uninitialized Core before start
findings.reproduction: db_core_create_v2 followed by snapshot/commit before db_core_start runs callSync inline in Manual state. config is only initialized in startOnLoop, but both new paths dereference it, including the commit error formatter. After stop snapshot produces an empty string.
findings.required_change: Guard the new APIs against unstarted/unavailable Core and return an explicit finite not_started result. Add actual C ABI before-start and after-stop cases without broadening unrelated legacy methods.

run_observations.interpretation: The invalid-batch fixture uses doors.front.call.return_s=-1, an undefined schema path accepted as an extension. It commits and causes cascading revision assertions. Use the real call.indoor.return_s field; this failure alone does not demonstrate rollback failure.

positive_inspection: HTTP and native conditional writes enter the same Core-loop service. The supplied revision is compared inside the Store recursive lock and SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE scope.
The LwwMap commit observer durably commits before rebuilding cfg, notifying UI or pushing config. A failed observer restores the pre-mutation map.
Store operation-ledger methods use the same recursive connection mutex; other-thread ledger operations cannot enter the conditional transaction. Nested configuration transaction scopes are rejected.
HTTP conditional commits require current admin session, random CSRF token and exact trusted Origin; the snapshot is no-store and strips the primary credential digest.
The opaque revision includes a boot/reset epoch plus the sorted complete local record identities, including tombstones. Legacy unconditional paths are explicitly documented as weaker.
limitations: The root agent owns execution and final source freezing. This initial review does not award production_test PASS or close any acceptance item.
Separate per-entity distributed conflict intent, editor migration, import staging, target hardware and final integration builds remain owned by their plan tasks.
